blocks.content: A drainage basin is an area of land drained by a main river and its tributaries, separated from neighboring basins by a elevated water divide.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India's drainage system is broadly divided into Himalayan Rivers (perennial) and Peninsular Rivers (seasonal/peninsular).
The major Himalayan river systems are the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra, characterized by deep V-shaped valleys and meanders.
Peninsular rivers such as Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi, and Cauvery flow eastwards into the Bay of Bengal, while Narmada and Tapti flow westwards into the Arabian Sea.
Drainage patterns like dendritic, radial, trellis, and rectangular are determined by underlying geological structure and topographical slope.

rows: Long courses with deep gorges and V-shaped valleys
Shorter courses with broad, shallow, mature valleys
East-flowing form deltas; West-flowing form estuaries

items: Godavari is the largest Peninsular river and is frequently referred to as 'Dakshin Ganga' in competitive exams.
Narmada and Tapti are major west-flowing rivers that run through rift valleys and form estuaries rather than deltas.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960, India gets exclusive rights over eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) while western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) are allocated mostly to Pakistan.
